newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Red flag to be raised over HK colonial mansion.
newsitem.headline: Red flag to be raised over HK colonial mansion.

text.p: Future Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa may have opted not to move into the mansion, but China's red flag will be hoisted over Government House, seat of the departing colonial governor, as soon as Beijing takes over.
The flag will go up on Tuesday over the neo-classical mansion, set on the slopes above Central Hong Kong among palm trees filled with squawking white parrots.
Chris Patten, Hong Kong's 28th and last British governor, has lived and worked there for the past five years as did his predecessors.
Tung, though, has decided not to move into the building, but to stay in his own apartment on the slopes above.

The red flag will also go up after midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday over Hong Kong airport, border checkpoints, court buildings, Tung's own office, central government offices, and the Legislative Council building in the downtown area.
Public transport vehicles will also fly the Chinese flag on holidays.
